newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude markets quiet, Brent paper eases lower.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude markets quiet, Brent paper eases lower.

text.p: Action was limited on the North Sea crude market on Monday morning, but some traders said that an easing of the backwardation on the Brent paper curve suggested that the physical market had a weaker undertone.
The Feb/Mar intermonth Brent spread was talked at +35/38 by midday having slipped from Friday's traded level of +44 cents to trade at +37 cents in the U.S. after-market.
Mar/Apr and Apr/May were also discussed lower at +38/42 cents.
March Brent paper was trading some 12 cents down at $22.13/$22.15 a barrel at 1315 GMT.
CFDs were also weaker but untraded.
Some traders felt that the market had peaked on Friday when benchmark Dated Brent traded at a high of March Brent +48 cents and other North Sea grades also changed hands at firm differentials.
"We felt it was the right time to sell on Friday," said the seller of a Gulfaks C cargo which fetched a premium of around 55 cents to Dated Brent.
But other traders believed the market had some further upside potential, particularly for gasoline-rich grades like Ekofisk, which traded three times on Friday.
A cargo loading Feb 5-7, the last of the delayed loadings from the January programme, was sold into Poland at around Dated Brent +30 cents.
Two mid-month cargoes were traded on a p+c basis at slightly higher differentials, traders said.
"The next asking prices for Ekofisk will be 35-40... I think it will get stronger," said one North Sea trader.
Two Brent cargoes were nominated from the paper chains on Monday.
In the Med, traders said the expected strengthening of differentials for Russian Urals had not materialised.
